summaries.demographer: Kweku Cooper is a 40-year-old African-American man living alone in a rented house in Blountstown, Florida, where he was also born and raised (Q11, Q51, Q87, Q89). He has never been married, has no children, and is not cohabiting with a romantic partner (Q05, Q84). His education is a high school diploma, and his main labor-market position is full-time retail sales work with about ten years at a regional department store (Q16, Q65, Q76, Q90). His household is single-person and economically modest but stable, with rent, utilities, vehicle costs, and groceries as core expenses (Q55-Q58, Q72-Q74).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Kweku shows strong loss aversion and precautionary budgeting: he tracks expenses, treats savings like a bill, avoids unnecessary debt, and could cover a $400 emergency but would feel the strain (Q57, Q61-Q63, Q82). His decisions prioritize stability, autonomy, and tangible returns, as seen in choosing work after high school and now considering short business courses for management mobility (Q02, Q18, Q108). He responds to incentives at work through sales goals and promotion prospects, but remains skeptical of vague promises from employers or politicians (Q16, Q24, Q65). His time preferences are practical: immediate bills come first, but he maintains long-term ambitions around supervision, home ownership, and possibly a convenience store (Q62, Q83, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Kweku is a moderate Democratic-leaning voter who participates in presidential elections and most midterms, with increasing attention to local government (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). His political views are shaped by working-class economics, rural underinvestment, health care access, racial fairness, and distrust of performative partisan conflict (Q24, Q25). He supports police accountability and takes Black Lives Matter concerns seriously, while also wanting effective public safety in his community (Q26-Q30). His civic style is quiet and relational rather than activist: he talks with family and trusted friends, volunteers one-on-one, and avoids social media conflict (Q17, Q29, Q48-Q49).
summaries.psychologist: Kweku presents as conscientious, independent, skeptical, and precision-oriented, with a strong preference for solitude after socially demanding retail work (Q11, Q42, Q65, Q109). He regulates stress through fishing, furniture restoration, cooking, budgeting, and online chess rather than substance use or public emotional disclosure (Q38-Q45, Q50). His self-concept centers on steadiness, competence, self-respect, and doing work correctly, and he is motivated by the wish to be seen as management-capable without losing autonomy (Q18, Q65, Q83, Q109). Relationally, he is loyal but bounded, maintaining family obligations and a small trusted circle while protecting quiet personal space (Q05-Q07, Q11).
